# SHORTLIST.md: the source-grounded shortlist (Chapter 7)
**Anisha Gaikar · JS3 · 2026-11-25.** Generated by `python3 tools/make_shortlist.py filters/filter_v1.0.json` (tables below) from the live collection of 14:11. The code is `js3/evidence.py`, and the rules are in FILTER.md §2.

## How a claim is labelled (FILTER.md §2, in code)
- **The claims.** For every posting the filter **kept**, the justification makes these claims:
  - the title is an entry-level analyst role;
  - one "requires X" claim for each skill word the filter matched;
  - "asks for at most 3 years".
- **The labels.** Each claim gets a label against the posting's **own text**, with the sentence quoted:
  - **SUPPORTED:** a sentence states it as a requirement or duty.
  - **CONTRADICTED:** the text says the opposite. For example, "5+ years" against "at most 3".
  - **INSUFFICIENT:** absent, or only *nice to have / a plus / preferred / bonus*, or under a "Preferred qualifications" heading.
- **Shortlisted** = the filter kept it **and** at least 2 skill claims are SUPPORTED **and** the years claim is not CONTRADICTED. **A posting is never shortlisted on a guess.**

**Result (v1.0):** 11 kept, **8 shortlisted**, 3 kept but **not** shortlisted.

## Relevance is not entailment: three real cases
Each posting below matches my words (the filter **kept** it: an analyst title plus 2 or more skill words), but the text does **not** support the claim that it requires those skills:

| Posting | What the words matched | What the text actually says | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Data Analyst, SF** (`greenhouse:stripe:8189909`) | SQL, Python | "Working knowledge of **Python**" sits under **"Preferred Qualifications"** | "requires Python" is INSUFFICIENT; only 1 skill is supported, so **not shortlisted** |
| **Credit Risk Operations Analyst** (`greenhouse:stripe:7456167`) | SQL, Excel | "Proficiency in **SQL**…" is under **"Preferred qualifications"**, and "Excel" is the verb in "You **excel** in diagnostic thinking" | **not shortlisted**. The Excel label is still wrong (see "My check" below). |
| **Processing Cost Analyst** (`greenhouse:stripe:8324207`) | SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, Excel (score 8, the top of the ranking) | Four of the five tools sit under **"Preferred qualifications"**, as "such as Power BI, Tableau, KNIME, Python, **or** Alteryx" (any one of them) | **not shortlisted**. The highest-scoring posting by word count is the clearest case of relevance without entailment. |

The real tool-server run on 2026-11-25 shows the same thing from the client's side. Claude Code, calling `score_posting` on Data Analyst SF, answered "the filter **kept** it… but `shortlist: false` because only one skill claim is backed by the text" (`transcripts/claude-run1-stream.jsonl`).

## The abstention rule and its limits
**The rule (FILTER.md §2):** the agent says **"I cannot tell"** instead of giving a verdict when:
- the posting text is missing;
- the text states no years at all (for the years claim);
- a skill appears only as INSUFFICIENT.

**Counterexample 1: it answers when it should abstain.**
- **The posting:** **Data Analyst, SF** says "MS or MA plus 2 years, or BS or BA plus 3 years, of full-time experience **exclusive of internships**".
- **What the agent does:** the largest number is 3, which is at most 3, so the years claim is **SUPPORTED** and the agent answers confidently.
- **Why that's wrong:** Nadia's only experience is a 1-year **internship**, so for her the honest answer is "she probably doesn't qualify." The rule abstains only when **no number** is stated. A number with a condition attached ("exclusive of internships", "or equivalent") passes as if it were a plain answer.

**Counterexample 2: it abstains when the answer is plain.**
- **Data Analyst, Intern** (two postings) states no years, so the years claim is "I cannot tell". But an internship plainly asks for no full-time years.
- **Operations Insights, Business Partner Analyst** says "**two (2) years** of related work experience". My years pattern reads only digits written right before "years", so "(2) years" is missed and the agent says "I cannot tell" when the text does tell.

**What these show:** the rule is keyed to the *surface form* of the text (is there a digit before "years"?), not to what the text *means* for this candidate. I did **not** fix the "(2) years" case in v1.1. That posting is in my held-out set, and changing the filter because of a held-out item would contaminate the measurement (WHAT_MOVES_THE_SCORE.md).

## My check of every label (49 claims)
- **Who checked:** Claude re-read every label against the posting text on 2026-11-25.
- **The labels I checked myself (Anisha):** I opened the 3 relevance≠entailment postings (gh_jid 8189909, 7456167, 8324207) on 11/25/2026 and confirmed each quote sits under "Preferred qualifications.".
- **Finding:** **4 labels are wrong, 2 are borderline, and 1 is right but misleading.** The labeller is a rule, not a reader.

| Posting | Claim | Label given | Should be | Why | Fixed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Credit Risk Operations Analyst | requires Excel | SUPPORTED | INSUFFICIENT | "You **excel** in…" is a verb, not the tool (**false friend**) | No. Found on a held-out item, so I recorded it and changed nothing |
| Financial Data Analyst Intern | at most 3 years | SUPPORTED | INSUFFICIENT | "At least 2 years of **university education**" is education, not experience (**false friend**) | **v1.1** (years followed by "education/university/degree" are ignored) |
| Software Engineer, Data Warehouse Analytics | entry-level analyst role | SUPPORTED | CONTRADICTED | "Analytics" in an engineering title (**false friend**) | **v1.1** (titles with "engineer" are rejected) |
| Operations Insights, Business Partner Analyst | at most 3 years | INSUFFICIENT | SUPPORTED | "two (2) years" is not read | No (held-out item) |
| FP&A Analyst R&D / FP&A Cloud Finance | requires Tableau / Snowflake | SUPPORTED | borderline | "**Become proficient** with… Tableau": a duty to *learn* it, not a requirement to *have* it | No: FILTER.md counts duties |
| Data Analyst, SF | at most 3 years | SUPPORTED | right but misleading | "exclusive of internships" (counterexample 1 above) | No |

**Before this check**, a bug in the labeller (a short bullet like "Experience with Oracle Suite" was taken for a heading and ended the "Preferred" section) had marked Processing Cost Analyst's preferred skills SUPPORTED and **shortlisted** it. I found it while re-reading. The order of the fix:
1. a regression test, written first and failing (`logs/06`, commit `017f3ca`);
2. then the fix, with 73/73 tests passing (`logs/07`, commit `6551bd8`).

v1.0 went from 9 shortlisted to **8**.
